description: stdcel/v1 — GENERIC, kro-style composer: a RESOURCE GRAPH DEFINITION expressed entirely as DATA. The providerconfig `spec` carries a `resources` list (each a child kind + a CEL-templated name/spec); the stdcel resource's OWN spec is the instance inputs, read in CEL as ${schema.spec.x}. Fields wire across the graph with CEL — ${other.spec.x} inlines a sibling's resolved spec at compose time, ${other.status.x} becomes a dependency edge + value flow (the engine schedules that resource first and flows its status in). The provider INFERS the dependency order from these references (topological), rejecting cycles/unknown/self references. One provider serves ANY composition with no code change — the generalisation of celbom (whose CEL is only a `when` selector over a fixed BOM fan-out). CEL is non-Turing-complete, so an operator-supplied graph is safe to run. Edit the graph + re-apply = recompose, no worker redeploy. Its child kinds must have their own applied CRDs; children DELETE with the root.

spec_schema.description: The INSTANCE inputs — the values a graph reads as ${schema.spec.*}. Shape is up to the graph author (kro's top-level schema); left open here so one stdcel kind can back many graphs.

config_schema.description: The RESOURCE GRAPH DEFINITION: the set of child resources and how their fields are wired with CEL. Structured, queryable JSON in the providerconfig spec — the point of the CEL approach vs an opaque program.

resources.description: The child graph. Declaration order is irrelevant — the provider infers the dependency order from the CEL references between resources.

id.description: Graph-local handle other resources reference in CEL as ${<id>.spec.x} / ${<id>.status.x}. Unique within the graph; never leaves the composer.

template.description: The child resource to compose. Every string leaf of name/spec/labels may carry ${...} CEL expressions over `schema.spec` (the instance) and sibling resources.

kind.description: Child resource kind to compose (must have an applied CRD).

kind_version.description: Child web-API version (v1, v2, …). REQUIRED — no implicit v1 default.

name.description: Child name — a CEL string template, e.g. "${schema.spec.name}-vpc".

spec.description: Child spec with CEL-expression leaves. A whole-value "${expr}" keeps the result's native type (int/bool/list/map); an interpolation "a-${expr}-b" is a string. A ${other.status.x} leaf is emitted as null and filled by the value flow at runtime.

labels.description: Extra labels stamped on the child (values may interpolate ${...}). The provider's own composed_by/graph_id labels win on a clash.
